html_source:
This short passage vividly illustrates the constant change of narrative perspectives that is prevalent in Ulysses.

We see Bloom trying to evade Blazes Boylan, more specifically the mere thought of him and Molly together. In constantly alternating mid-sentence between a third-person narrator and his inner thoughts, Bloom’s displacement activity gains a thrilling immediacy.

I am looking for that. Yes, that. Try all pockets. Handker. Freeman. Where did I? Ah, yes. Trousers. Purse. Potato. Where did I? 

 Hurry. Walk quietly. Moment more. My heart.
